profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers. Per the operator's own site, Iron Mountain's global data center portfolio spans more than 30 locations across three continents totaling roughly 1.4 GW of capacity.

This facility, AZP-2, is part of Iron Mountain's roughly 39-acre Phoenix campus at 4802 East Van Buren Street, Phoenix, Arizona, alongside AZP-1 and a third building, AZP-3, which the operator's own site names but which is not separately tracked as a row in this registry. AZP-1 and AZP-2's on-file addresses are roughly 1.5 to 2 miles apart, so this registry treats them as separate parcels under a shared campus marketing umbrella rather than one contiguous physical footprint, pending clearer confirmation. The Phoenix campus is linked by a 100 Gbps dark-fiber ring to Iron Mountain's separate, roughly 4.5-acre Scottsdale campus (AZS-1). Per the operator, AZP-2 itself carries 48 MW of IT capacity, and the combined Phoenix-plus-Scottsdale footprint totals more than 130 MW across 50-plus acres and 1.4 million-plus square feet.

Iron Mountain's 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers added four colocation facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two in Arizona, per Wikipedia's account of the deal; this registry has not located a primary source this session confirming whether AZP-2 specifically was one of the two acquired Arizona sites or a later Iron Mountain build. No year-opened figure, standalone square footage for this building alone, or independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate was located in sourcing to date.

Iron Mountain trades on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker IRM and files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under CIK 0001020569, structured as a real estate investment trust. Records management remains the company's larger, founding business line by facility count; the data center segment is reported separately in Iron Mountain's public filings as a smaller but faster-growing division. Metro Phoenix has grown into one of the largest US data center markets outside the traditional Northern Virginia and Dallas hubs, drawing operators in part on lower land costs and a large regional power grid footprint.

reading.body:
AZP-2 is one building on Iron Mountain's Phoenix campus, which the operator states holds 48 MW of IT capacity at this address on Van Buren Street. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that translates roughly to 1,200 racks. The broader Phoenix campus, including AZP-1 and AZP-3, totals more than 130 MW across 50 acres and 1.4 million square feet, connected by dark fiber to a separate Scottsdale facility 4.5 miles away. Year opened and certifications for this specific building are not published.

AZP-2 ranks fifth among Arizona's four facilities with published capacity figures, holding 9 percent of the state's 512 MW of disclosed IT power. Arizona has 56 mapped data center sites total, but most publish no capacity; Phoenix has become a major US market outside Northern Virginia and Dallas, drawing operators partly on lower land costs and regional grid scale. Iron Mountain's global portfolio totals roughly 1.4 GW across 30 locations, making this facility a small piece of a larger operator footprint.

Iron Mountain is a publicly traded real estate investment trust built primarily on physical records management, with data centers as a growing but smaller division. Whether AZP-2 dates from the company's 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers or a later build is not published. The campus connectivity and multibuilding scale suggest it is designed for wholesale or hyperscale tenancy, though no operator announcements of specific tenants were found in available sources.
